correctness.rationale: For every finite simple graph and real a, Walsh parity leaves only repeated edges and simple four-cycles, giving E F⁴=3S²−2Σa_e⁴+24Σ_CΠ_Ca_e. When cycles are pairwise edge-disjoint the exact rearrangement of 4S²−E F⁴ consists of a nonnegative global mass defect S²−Σ_Cs_C²+2Σ_outside a_e⁴ and nonnegative single-cycle AM–GM defects s_C²+2Σ_Ca_e⁴−24Π_Ca_e. Equality forces one uniform signed-positive square; when there are no squares, Cauchy gives 3−2/m, all magnitudes equal, and an L⁴ isometry to independent signs. For near-optimizers Σs_C²≥1−δ gives t=max s_C/S>1/2 and δ≥2t(1−t); disjoint two-square coefficients attain the threshold. These are all-size analytic conclusions, not extrapolations of finite checks.

General hypercontractive norm comparisons and four-cycle counts in asymptotic graph chaos do not give this all-coefficient equality/localization theorem. Published Q3 cube edge-Walsh theorem has the same scalar optimum and face-support extremizers for ONE graph with overlapping squares, not for all graphs whose four-cycles have disjoint edges. Graph moment identity itself is well known and NOT claimed novel.
